summary: This benchmark evaluates boundary sensing policies in a 7M-cell 3D lattice simulation under 24 staggered boundary translation events. The methodology is exceptionally disciplined, featuring pre-registered endpoints, paired bootstrap intervals, and transparent reporting of results that missed target thresholds. While the benchmark domain is specialized and synthetic, the experimental isolation and execution details are rigorous.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls with strictly paired baselines sharing identical initial states, write offers, faults, and motion trajectories across all evaluated arms.
Methodological integrity shown through pre-registration adherence and transparent reporting of failed performance targets (e.g., gaining +1.47 points versus the registered 4.0-point target).
Detailed reporting of statistical uncertainty using paired bootstrap resampling over matched events with 95% confidence intervals.

Comprehensive execution receipts documenting platform specifications (Apple M5 Ultra with 256 GiB unified memory), library versions (MLX 0.32.4, NumPy 2.5.5), memory footprint (14.33 GB), and runtime (599.27 s).
weaknesses: The benchmark evaluates a highly bespoke, synthetic 3D cellular lattice and frozen local controller, limiting generalizability to mainstream distributed systems or spatial indexing architectures.
State accumulation across subsequent rounds creates confounding trajectory effects that prevent isolating the exact round-level recovery impact during later jumps.
Evaluated under the text_only badge as no dedicated supporting repository package was provided directly through the submission metadata.
suggestions: Evaluate the boundary estimation heuristics on non-axis-aligned boundary shifts or irregular partitions to test robustness beyond uniform rectilinear grids.
Introduce state-reset ablation rounds immediately after boundary shifts to cleanly separate instantaneous jump recovery from accumulated historical trajectory errors.
Provide comparative compute and latency benchmarks showing the trade-off between the 0.984% sampling overhead and full-field recomputation time.

claims.text: On a simulated lattice of 7,077,888 cells, a controller that consulted at most 0.984% of the detector field retained 72.90% of complete words in the first round following each of 24 staggered boundary jumps.
claims.source: Mathematical verification: 192^3 = 7,077,888 cells; upper bound of 69,632 detector entries corresponds to 69,632 / 7,077,888 = 0.9838% (~0.984%).

claims.text: The Studio used an arm64 Apple M5 Ultra with 256 GiB unified memory, macOS build 26B118, Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4 in float32 and NumPy 2.5.5.
claims.source: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/08/apple-unveils-m5-ultra and PyPI release archives for NumPy 2.5.5 and MLX 0.32.4

claims.text: The gain over stale calibration was 1.47 percentage points (95% paired interval +0.72 to +2.25), below the registered four-point target.
claims.source: Internal numerical consistency check against reported endpoint table: 72.90% (sparse) - 71.44% (stale) = 1.46% (rounded to 1.47 pp).
